main_body: Timber-frame farmhouse: a large tiled roof slope (rows 3-53) with a dormer, above a plaster and timber front wall with a large double barn door and two small windows (rows 55-90)
top_band: Roof tile slope, rows 3-53: cream ridge highlight on rows 3-4, then orange/red/plum tile rows. The step to the front face is the dark eave shadow at rows 54-55, then the cream plaster wall.
evidence: The roof is drawn as a big sloped surface with a lit ridge row and per-tile highlights. It overhangs the wall and casts a dark eave shadow at rows 54-55, with the wall face set back below it. The wall has its own timber frame and a door with a lintel beam. The dormer has a sill and an inset window with a dark top edge. This matches the Beodeul house references, where the roof slope is the top surface above the front wall. No receding side faces appear.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 tile tones plus a cream highlight, with scalloped per-tile highlights. The plaster has speckle, and the doors have plank grain, braces and nails. Outlines are brown or plum tinted (1% near-neutral dark edge pixels). Median 21 colours per tile beats both references (18 and 11), and flat-fill coverage is 0%. It holds up next to the references and does not look thinner or more sticker-like.
